Commentary.Commentary: West Indies will be disappointed more with that middle phase than the final one as the batsmen did not have time to slog. But that period from overs 6-11, the batsmen struggled to get going and could not score off the spinners. The trio of Hamza, Nabi and Rashid went for 46 runs in 7 overs with a wicket. Stay tuned for Afghanistan's reply.

It was a poor start with the ball again from Afghanistan, as they conceded 51 runs in the first 5 overs. But after that, they put brakes on the proceedings as the next 6 yielded only 28 runs. Then rain arrived before the final shootout.
Not a bad finish from Afghanistan. Jut 33 runs came in the final 4 overs. The target will be re-adjusted according to the DLS method. Will let you know about the same.
A short ball outside off, slower in pace, dragged down to long on for a couple. WEST INDIES FINISH ON 112/3!
A fine yorker outside off, Brathwaite misses his attempted dig. The keeper fumbles and the batsmen sneak in a bye.
Noor Ali Zadran is leaving the field to have his shoulder attended to.

Banged in short around off, Simmons back away to the leg side, swings early to the leg side and gets a top edge. The ball goes high in the air and Noor Ali Zadran comes charging in from the mid-wicket fence but is unable to get to the ball. Falls awkwardly on his left shoulder and in the meanwhile, the batsmen take two. The throw is a wild one, right in the middle of the pitch and the third is taken as well.
Short and wide outside off, pulled down to long on for a single. Again, would have been a wide had it been left alone.
The ball has been lost and a replacement is being called for.
SIX! WHAM! A nice juicy full toss on off as Dawlat misses his yorker length and Brathwaite dispatches it from his presence with a swing over mid-wicket.
Full and wide outside off, could have been left alone, but Brathwaite goes after it without moving his feet and gets a bottom edge back to the bowler.
DAWLAT ZADRAN to bowl the final over.
Comes down the track, backs away to the leg side, Naib bowls it wide outside off, Simmons swings but misses.
On a good length around off, gently worked towards cover for a single.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
CARLOS BRATHWAITE walks in at number 4, replacing Samuels.

OUT! The slowness of the pitch induces a wicket. The length is full, the line if following the batsman around leg as he backs away to the l;eg side, Samuels attempts a big hit over long on but the ball hits the toe end of the bat and goes to Najibullah Zadran at the long on fence.
Another yorker, outside off, Samuels looks to play a back foot drive but misses.
Excellent yorker, right on middle, can only be driven back to the bowler.
Simmons calls for a helmet as NAIB continues...
Short and outside off, cut behind point for a couple.
FOUR! Slightly short from Rashid, Simmons punches on it, going back and heaving it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Landed outside off, the googly, spins in, punched through point for another single.
Full on middle, clipped through mid-wicket for one.
Punches this through the off side for a run.
Around middle, worked to the leg side for a single.
RASHID KHAN to bowl out.
SIX! Spoils a good over. Full and slightly around off, Samuels gets underneath this and sends the ball sailing down the ground!
Full on leg stump, pushed down to long on for a run.
Very full again, driven to the off side.
Full and just arou8nd off, pushed back to the bowler.
Follows the batsman down the leg side as he looks to make room, there is some swing from Samuels, but the ball goes off the inside half of the bat to deep square leg. Just a single.
Excellent start. Full and very straight, driven back to the bowler.

Welcome back, folks! Action is all set to resume. The match has been reduced to 15-OVERS-A-SIDE. Afghanistan's target will be adjusted according to the DLS method. Maximum of 3 overs per bowler and the Afghans will have a Powerplay of 5 overs. GULBADIN NAIB will resume proceedings to MARLON SAMUELS. Here we go...

2200 local update - GOOD NEWS! The rain has stopped completely and all covers have been removed from the ground. The players are doing their warm-ups, which means play could start anytime soon. Only question would be the status of the outfield, as to how good is it to take play. Stay tuned...

2130 local update - Thee ground staff is getting together near the pitch but there seems to be a bit of a drizzle still. The Super Sopper is on the cover, flushing out lots of water but other than that not much activity. We are already in the process of the overs getting deducted.
It seems to be really pouring down here. Puddles have already formed. Doesn't look like stopping very soon.
Well, the heavens have opened up and the crowd is running for shelter. This does not look like a passing shower. The umpires have called in for the covers. Only one in place though.
Full and outside off, blocked solidly towards cover.
On the pads, worked through square leg for a single.
Quicker delivery, very straight, Marlon defends.
This time he stays back and blocks.
The googly outside off, a tentative Samuels pokes it towards cover.
Landed outside off, punched towards point.
Backs away to the leg side and punches it through point for another single.
Works this through mid-wicket for one.
Backs away to the leg side again, the bowler keeps it fuller, slower and closer to his legs, Marlon can only heave it to widish long on for a run.
A lovely delivery, a terrific yorker on leg stump, Samuels, backing away to the leg side for a big inside-out shot, has to defend.
On a good length around off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
LENDL SIMMONS walks in at number 4, replacing Lewis.

OUT! Straight to the man. A short ball, around middle, Lewis looks to pull and does so, but does not get the correct elevation. The timing is excellnt but the target is Gulbadin Naib instead of the ropes at the mid-wicket fence. Simple catch.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Full and down the leg side, swept through fine leg for a couple.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full on middle, driven towards mid on.
RASHID KHAN to bowl now.
The ball strikes the batsman very low on the pads The batsmen have run through for a single. The umpire signals a leg bye.
A better delivery, yorker outside off, Lewis misses to dig it out.
FIVE WIDES! Poor keeping. A bad ball to start, miles outside off, Lewis leaves it alone. Shafiqullah gets around to his left to stop but the ball hits his left leg and races to the fine leg fence.
Around off, punched towards mid off.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
A length ball outside off, Samuels flays at that flat-footed, aiming to go over covers and misses big time.
On a good length around off, punched through the covers for a single.
KARIM JANAT is back into the attack.
On middle and leg again, punched down to long on for a single. 11 from the over.
On middle and leg, worked through square leg for a brace.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A quicker and shorter one on off, punched down to long off for a run.
SIX! WHACK! A bit of loop around middle, from around the wicket, Samuels leans and whips it massively over deep mid-wicket. That was right in the slot.
Full and around off, pushed through to long off for a single.
Comes down the track and defends. Excellent finish to the Powerplay. Just 1 from it.
Darted on middle and leg, Samuels misses his tuck and is hit on the pads. Going down leg.
Full and just around off, watchfully pushed back.
Fullish around off, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Comes down the track and flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside leg, Lewis looks to sweep but misses the ball and is hit on the p[ads. Hamza puts in a valiant appeal but that cannot be given.
On a good length outside off, Samuels lunges and punches this through the covers. The fielders give it a good chase and work in pairs to stop the ball. Two runs taken.
Great work. Shortish on middle, Lewis turns this around the corner. It has good timing and seems to be racing to the ropes but Amir Hamza gets around and stops it cleanly. Just a single.
SIX! WALLOP! Tossed up outside off, Lewis comes down the track and lofts this miles over extra cover!
MARLON SAMUELS walks in at number 3, replacing Walton.

OUT! There comes the first wicket. Full and outside off, Walton looks to loft it over long on but is not able to get enough on it. He finds Noor Ali Zadran running to his left from long on to take the catch. Losing just a little bit of concentration there, Walton, amidst all the drama.
Lewis is in some pain here. The physio is out in the middle, tending to him. The batsman seemed to be in a lot of pain but has eventually got ready to resume. Might have been a bit shaken up.

OOPS.... WATCH IT! Massive collision. On the pads, Lewis flicked it towards short fine leg. He did not want the single but Walton called him into it. The keeper went after it quickly as the batsmen took the single and had a shy at the bowler's end. Meanwhile, Lewis, who was ball-watching, ran full steam into SAMIULLAH SHENWARI who had come in as a backup from short extra cover. He was watching the ball as well and collided into Lewis. Both fell down.
Full on middle and off, watchfully defended towards mid on for a quick single.
Another bowling change. MOHAMMAD NABI is going to come on.
A tad short around off, Walton goes back and punches it wide of long on for a single. 10 from that over, 21 off the last 2!
SIX! VIOLENCE! Right on top of the roof! Flighted outside off, Walton comes forward and launches this miles over long off!
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a single.
Down the leg side, Lewis misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
AMIR HAMZA to bowl now.
Outside off, pushed towards cover for a quick single. The fielder comes charging in and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Walton was in though.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Good shot but a poor piece of fielding. Full and outside off, Lewis leans and drives this on the up through the covers. The fielder gets across to his left and slides but the ball goes beneath his arms and races to the fence.
A short ball, pulled away for a single.
On a good length around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
FOUR! Now that is a poor ball. A short ball, around middle, Walton pulls it behind square leg and gets a boundary. He is in a hurry.
On a good length around off, Chadwick pushes at it but gets a thick inside edge towards short fine leg.
WIDE. Down the leg side, left alone.
Full on middle and leg, Lewis tries to work it away but misses and is hit on the pads. Inside edge saves him.
Pushes this towards mid on for a quick single.
FOUR! This time he finds the gap. Banged in short and outside off, Walton pulls it wide of mid-wicket and gets a boundary!
A short ball around off, Walton pulls it past a diving mid-wicket for a couple.
On a good length around off, defended back to the bowler.
Full on middle, worked towards short fine leg for a single.
KARIM JANAT to bowl from the other end.
FOUR! Off the top edge! A short ball around middle, Walton swivels for the pull but gets a top edge which goes over the keeper to the fine leg fence!
WIDE. The batsman tries flicking a ball that is down the leg side. The umpire signals a wide.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
A bouncer, Lewis ducks.
Short and wide outside off, Walton shoulders arms. The keeper fumbles and the batsmen take a bye.
FOUR! Short and around middle, Walton pulls this over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Outside off, played uppishly but straight to point. Lands just short.
The players are out in the middle. It will be Chadwick Walton and Evin Lewis to open the innings. DAWLAT ZADRAN has the new cherry in his hand. Walton to face. Here we go...
TOSS - The start was delayed due to a brief shower just before the start of the game but we are now ready to begin. West Indies HAVE ELECTED TO BAT.

It was a totally one-sided encounter as Afghanistan's record winning streak in T20Is came to a halt in what was an unkind manner to the visitors. The batting never came to understanding the pitch and as a result,   they were out of the contest in the first half itself. Come the second game, they will be looking to give a better display and give the Windies a run for their money. The hosts, on the other hand, will aim to seal the   series tonight itself and show some consistency. Hello and a warm welcome to the second T20I between West Indies and Afghanistan at Basseterre.
